label: token right after an early q (q at position 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, on the input immediately after a q when that q is the first or second original token (t = 1 or 2). Strongest (~0.9-1.0 of max, about 90% of activation mass) at t = 1 when the sequence starts with q, nearly regardless of the current token. At t = 2 (q in position 1) it is weak (~0.1-0.4 of max) and fires on only ~63% of such steps. Never fires after a q at later positions, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase, even when q is input again during recall.

issues: The factual claims hold up. Activity is 100% in the original phase, with zero activations at the delimiter or in the copy phase. It fires only at t=1 (90.4% of activation mass) and t=2 (9.6%). The predicate misses nothing on the test split (recall 1.0).

At t=1 the predicate (prev_tok==q, t==1) has precision 1.0 on test. Every sequence starting with q fires, whatever the current token is, so the claim that the current token barely matters is confirmed.

Systematic gap: all 6154 test false positives are at t=2, and whether the feature fires there is decided almost entirely by the first original token (first_tok), not by noise. Firing rate for the t=2 subset by first_tok: a, b, e, q, v, w, z are 0.0; s is 0.025; 3 is 0.10; k is 0.13. Meanwhile c, d, f, h, i, l, n, o, p, r, x, y, 0, 2 are 1.0, and 1 is 0.97. The explanation calls the t=2 case a 63% partial firing and never names this deterministic dependence on the first token.
Other candidate factors at t=2 have little effect. Current token is digit: 0.62. L<=5: 0.62. L>=7: 0.63. in_tok==q: 0.48. First token is a digit: 0.76.
skeptic.revised_label: token right after an early q: always at t=1 (sequence starts with q); at t=2 only when the first token is not one of a/b/e/q/v/w/z/k/s/3

final_label: token right after an early q: always at t=1 (sequence starts with q); at t=2 only when the first token is not one of a/b/e/q/v/w/z/k/s/3
